Q: How to empty a single column in MySQL without updating each row individually? A: 
CREATE TABLE `t` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `v` varchar(10) DEFAULT NULL,
  `vv` int DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB AUTO_INCREMENT=519 DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci

alter table t add vvvv int

alter table t drop column vv

alter table  t rename column vvvv to vv

Q: Problems compiling code with cmake and Boost / OpenCV A:

The issue is manifested by presence of things like std::__debug::vector in the names of undefined symbols. These are debug-iterator versions of STL's containers as implemented in gcc's libstdc++. They are ABI-incompatible with "usual" non-instrumented versions of same containers so gcc developers have put them into their own namespace (so incorrect mixing of the two results in compile-time issue rather than hard-to-debug runtime bugs). In this particular example, there is an ABI mismatch between application (which uses debug iterators) and boost precompiled library (which does not).

Now, why does the application uses them and how OpenCV ties into this? Verbose build logs show that -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG (which is the thing that enabled debug iterators) is added to the compilation line as soon as OpenCV libraries are "linked" to the application. That option comes from OpenCVModule.cmake installed with this particular OpenCV installation. Why would OpenCV force this flag onto its users? Thing is, it could optionally be built with debug iterators if specifically requested by ENABLE_GNU_STL_DEBUG (OpenCV compile time) option. As said before, debug iterators are ABI-incompatible so OpenCV tries to be helpful by ensuring library users are compatible with OpenCV.

As with other ABI-incompatible changes, all of the C++ code has to be compiled in the same mode including all the shared libraries. Failure to do so would result in build errors like seen in this case.

Q: Papaparse "Duplicate headers found and renamed" with no duplicate headers A:

One thing I noticed is that it happens with very big files, when they are more batches. in fact if I set batch size to 1000 it disappears. or if I only have 499 rows. So I think it might be a parsing problem tied to the batch import when using `step()`.

Q: using sed to replace multiple lines between two patterns A:

This might work for you (GNU sed):

sed '/BEGIN/{:a;N;/END/!ba;s#.*#echo "&"|sed "3~2s/./X/g"#e}' file

Slurp up the lines between BEGIN and END and pass them to a second invocation of sed using the e flag of the substitution command.

The above idiom applies to all cases, however for the specific example mentioned by the OP:

sed '/BEGIN/{:a;n;/END/b;n;//b;s/./X/g;ba}' file

would also be suffice.

Q: Trying to connect to salesforce from Postman Salesforce but failing with authentication failure A:

  1. Go to Setup in Salesforce.

  2. Search for OAuth and OpenID Connect Settings.

  3. Verify that the relevant flows are enabled.

  4. Check the Connected App configuration:

    Relax IP restrictions if necessary.

    Ensure the app is enabled for the profile you are working with.

  5. Confirm that the credentials are correct:

    Username

    Password

    Auth URL

    Token URL

I hope these steps help in resolving the issue.
